newsitem.title: USA: Clinton launches attack ad on Dole.
newsitem.headline: Clinton launches attack ad on Dole.

text.p: President Clinton's re-election campaign aired a new television ad Friday attacking Republican challenger Bob Dole on his proposed tax cut plan, the centrepiece of his campaign.

The spot running in various markets attempts to portray Dole as voting for tax hikes before he left the Senate and proposing now a "risky tax scheme" that would have to cut Medicare health care for the elderly to help pay for it.

The Dole campaign did not have an immediate response. Dole has proposed an across-the-board 15 percent personal income tax rate cut and capital gains tax reductions in an economic package he estimated will reduce revenues $548 billion over six years, but he has not detailed how he would finance it to keep his promise to balance the budget.

Clinton campaign spokesman Joe Lockhart said the advertisement would run in "battleground states" but would not elaborate. It is designed to counter a Dole ad accusing the president of guiding the largest tax hike in history in 1993.
"Bob Dole, attacking the president. But President Clinton cut taxes for 15 million families, 10 million new jobs, proposes tax credits for college.
"Dole voted to raise payroll taxes. Social Security taxes. The '90 income tax increase - 900 billion in higher taxes.
"And to help pay for his risky tax scheme, experts say Dole and (House Speaker Newt) Gingrich will have to cut Medicare, education, environment.
"Bob Dole. Raising taxes. Trying to cut Medicare. Running from his record."
